answer.rationale: A release landed ~2 hours ago and the p99 write-path latency has been climbing for 90 minutes of that window — the temporal correlation is strong and no other concurrent change is indicated. memory_b1 records a directly analogous situation (post-release checkout error spike) where rollback resolved the issue cleanly with no customer impact. At day 74 settlement peak, writes are heavy and customer-facing; a 5× p99 overshoot will soon start timing out commits. Rolling back restores the last-known-good build while preserving the write path. Regional failover (memory_b2) addresses a prior latency-degradation event but not a code regression; circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect downstream dependencies, not our own write path; read-replica routing (memory_b5) offloads reads, not the write path under stress; adding capacity (not in memory) would mask the defect without fixing it and delays diagnosis. If the rollback does not flatten the p99 curve within 15–20 minutes, the next intervention window should revisit regional failover or circuit-breaker options.
